functional_requirements.requirement: The system shall enable customers to browse and search for grocery items within the defined hyperlocal delivery zone.
functional_requirements.business_need: Customers need immediate access to available products without manual location verification to reduce cart abandonment.
functional_behaviour: System shall display a geofenced product catalog based on the user's current or selected delivery address.
Search interface shall support text-based queries, category filtering, and brand filtering.
Item cards shall display real-time stock availability and estimated delivery time.
System shall auto-calculate delivery fees based on the distance between warehouse and customer.
related_information_requirements: Customer GPS coordinates or manually entered address
business_rules: A product must be displayed only if its inventory is greater than zero at the assigned warehouse.
A product must be displayed only if the assigned warehouse is within the maximum delivery radius for the customer's address.

acceptance_criteria.given: The customer is located at coordinates (Lat: 1.3521, Long: 103.8198) and the warehouse is at (Lat: 1.3500, Long: 103.8200) with a 2km radius rule.
acceptance_criteria.when: The customer searches for a product assigned to that warehouse.
acceptance_criteria.then: The product is displayed in the catalog with an estimated delivery time.

acceptance_criteria.given: The warehouse has 5 units of Product X in stock.
acceptance_criteria.when: The customer adds Product X to the cart and attempts to proceed to checkout.
acceptance_criteria.then: The checkout process allows payment, and the cart reflects 5 units.

acceptance_criteria.given: The warehouse has 0 units of Product Y in stock.
acceptance_criteria.when: The customer searches for Product Y.
acceptance_criteria.then: Product Y is either not displayed or marked as 'Out of Stock' with a 'Notify Me' option.

functional_requirements.requirement: The system shall process orders and assign them to delivery personnel dynamically based on proximity and capacity.
functional_requirements.business_need: To maintain the 'Quick Commerce' promise of <15-30 minute delivery, the system must automate the dispatch logic to minimize handover time.
functional_behaviour: System shall calculate the optimal delivery route by considering the warehouse location and the customer's address.
System shall match available riders to orders based on the shortest estimated travel time and rider capacity.
System shall update the customer's order status (e.g., 'Picking', 'Out for Delivery', 'Arrived') in real-time.
System shall provide live tracking visualization on the customer's mobile app.
business_rules: An order cannot be assigned to a rider who is currently assigned to another active delivery exceeding maximum load capacity.
The system must prioritize orders with shorter estimated delivery windows first.
If no rider is available within the acceptance window, the order shall be queued for the next available slot and the customer notified.

acceptance_criteria.given: Three orders are pending assignment within a 1km radius of a single warehouse.
acceptance_criteria.when: The system runs the assignment algorithm and a rider located 500m from the warehouse becomes available.
acceptance_criteria.then: The rider is assigned the closest order first, and subsequent orders are assigned in order of priority.

acceptance_criteria.given: A rider is en route to a customer's address.
acceptance_criteria.when: The customer opens the app to track the order.
acceptance_criteria.then: The app displays the rider's live location and an ETA that updates every 30 seconds.

acceptance_criteria.given: All riders within a 5km radius are at maximum capacity.
acceptance_criteria.when: A new high-priority order is placed.
acceptance_criteria.then: The system queues the order and sends a notification to the customer that the delivery will be delayed until the next rider shift.

functional_requirements.requirement: The system shall manage inventory synchronization between the warehouse management system (WMS) and the customer-facing platform.
functional_requirements.business_need: Inaccurate stock levels are critical in Q-Commerce as they directly impact customer satisfaction and order fulfillment failure rates.
functional_behaviour: System shall deduct inventory immediately upon successful order confirmation.
System shall trigger a restock alert when a SKU reaches the minimum threshold.
System shall handle inventory adjustments for returns and cancellations instantly.
System shall prevent the sale of items if the warehouse stock goes below zero during the checkout process.
related_information_requirements: Current physical stock count per SKU per warehouse
business_rules: Inventory count = Physical Stock - Pending Orders + Returns.
If physical stock is updated by warehouse staff, the customer-facing count must update within 60 seconds.
Orders for out-of-stock items must be cancelled automatically before payment finalization.

acceptance_criteria.given: A warehouse staff member adjusts the stock of Item Z from 10 to 5 units.
acceptance_criteria.when: The system syncs with the database after the adjustment is saved.
acceptance_criteria.then: The customer-facing catalog updates to show 5 units available for Item Z within 60 seconds.

acceptance_criteria.given: The customer adds Item Z (5 units left) to the cart and attempts to add 6 units.
acceptance_criteria.then: The system limits the quantity to 5 units and prevents checkout with 6 units.

acceptance_criteria.given: An order for Item Z (5 units) is confirmed and being picked up.
acceptance_criteria.when: The customer cancels the order before the rider picks it up.
acceptance_criteria.then: The system immediately adds 5 units back to the available inventory.

functional_requirements.requirement: The system shall handle order anomalies including missed pickups, failed deliveries, and customer refunds.
functional_requirements.business_need: Robust exception handling is required to ensure revenue protection and maintain trust when the 'quick' delivery fails.
functional_behaviour: System shall allow riders to report a 'Missed Delivery' or 'Customer Not Home' via the app.
System shall automatically trigger a rescheduling workflow for failed deliveries.
System shall process partial refunds if only some items in the order are missing.
System shall generate a refund request ticket for the customer service team.
business_rules: A delivery is considered 'Failed' only after 2 or 3 unsuccessful attempts.
Refunds for missing items shall be processed within 24 hours of verification.
The rider is not penalized financially for a missed delivery caused by incorrect address data provided by the customer.

acceptance_criteria.given: A rider attempts to deliver an order but the customer is not home.
acceptance_criteria.when: The rider marks the delivery as 'Failed' and uploads a photo of the location.
acceptance_criteria.then: The system updates the order status to 'Rescheduling Required' and sends a push notification to the customer.

acceptance_criteria.given: An order contains 5 items, but 2 items are missing upon rider arrival.
acceptance_criteria.when: The rider reports the issue and the system verifies the warehouse stock.
acceptance_criteria.then: The system calculates the cost of the 2 missing items and initiates a partial refund to the customer.

acceptance_criteria.given: The customer provides an incorrect address leading to a failed delivery.
acceptance_criteria.when: The rider reports the issue and the customer confirms the address error.
acceptance_criteria.then: The system waives the late delivery fee from the rider and does not apply a penalty to the rider's performance score.

functional_requirements.requirement: The system shall provide a merchant dashboard for warehouse staff to manage picking and packing efficiency.
functional_requirements.business_need: Warehouse efficiency is the bottleneck in Q-Commerce; the system must optimize the picking process to reduce order fulfillment time.
functional_behaviour: System shall generate optimized picking lists based on item proximity within the warehouse.
System shall provide real-time visibility of pending orders vs. completed orders.
System shall allow staff to scan barcodes/QR codes to confirm item picking.
System shall alert staff when a high-priority rush order is placed.
related_information_requirements: Current warehouse layout and bin locations
business_rules: Rush orders must be flagged in the picking list and prioritized in the queue.
A picker must confirm the picking of an item before moving to the next item in the list.
An order cannot be marked as 'Ready for Dispatch' until all items in the picking list are confirmed.

acceptance_criteria.given: A rush order is placed containing Item A and Item B.
acceptance_criteria.when: The picker opens the picking list on the handheld device.
acceptance_criteria.then: The system highlights Item A and Item B with a 'Rush' tag and places them at the top of the list.

acceptance_criteria.given: The picker scans the barcode of Item C which is located in Bin 12.
acceptance_criteria.when: The system validates the scan against the order.
acceptance_criteria.then: The system confirms the scan, updates the inventory deduction, and allows the picker to proceed to the next item.

acceptance_criteria.given: The picker attempts to mark an order as 'Ready' after picking only 2 out of 3 items.
acceptance_criteria.when: The picker clicks the 'Complete Order' button.
acceptance_criteria.then: The system blocks the action and displays an error message: 'Missing 1 item from order #12345'.
